subject: Predicted probabilities of a binary (ordinal) indicator (lavPredict, type="fy")

messages.author: 5a2f8b4089c81b75
messages.subject: Predicted probabilities of a binary (ordinal) indicator (lavPredict, type="fy")
parts:
Hi All,

Would anyone know how to obtain the predicted probabilities of a binary (ordinal) indicator from a fitted model, please?

An MWE is as follows:
----
N <- 1e3
X <- rnorm(N)
Y <- rbinom(N,1,exp(X)/(1+exp(X)))
D <- data.frame(X,Y)
model <- '
Y ~ X
'
fit <- lavaan::sem(model,data=D,ordered=TRUE,link="probit")
fit@Model@link
lavPredict(fit,type="fy",se="none")

----
I encountered this error message: "Error in dimnames(x) <- dn :
length of 'dimnames' [2] not equal to array extent"

Any help or suggestions on resolving this would be much appreciated. Thanks!

Wen Wei

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Predicted probabilities of a binary (ordinal) indicator (lavPredict, type="fy")
parts:
On 10/4/22 06:32, Wen L. wrote:
> Would anyone know how to obtain the predicted probabilities of a binary
> (ordinal) indicator from a fitted model, please?

I am afraid you can't. lavPredict() does not produce predicted
probabilities (or other yhat values) as in regular (generalized) linear
models.

lavPredict's sole purpose is to produce factor scores, and quantities
derived from these factor scores. In doing that, it ignores the
structural part of the model (by design). It is pretty much useless for
models with no latent variables.

The only way forward is manually. For your model, you can get the usual
'linear predictor' as follows:

linpred <- drop(cbind(-1,X) %*% coef(fit)[c(2,1)])

which can be converted to probabilities using pnorm():

pnorm(linpred)

Yves.
